vasp.notes: This calculation will fully relax bulk silicon (cell shape, volume, and ionic positions) using ISIF=3. Silicon is a semiconductor with a bandgap, so ISMEAR=0 (Gaussian smearing) with SIGMA=0.05 eV is appropriate for the relaxation. The structure provided is the conventional cubic cell of diamond-structure Si with 8 atoms. An 8×8×8 Gamma-centered k-point mesh provides good convergence for Si (approximately 0.025 Å⁻¹ spacing). ENCUT=450 eV is more than sufficient for Si (default ENMAX ~250 eV). After the calculation completes, the optimized cubic lattice constant can be read from the final lattice vectors in the CONTCAR file - all three diagonal elements should be equal (within numerical noise) for the cubic structure. The experimental lattice constant for Si is ~5.43 Å; PBE typically overestimates it by ~1-2%. For production-quality results, you may want to increase the k-point mesh to 10×10×10 or 12×12×12 and verify convergence with respect to ENCUT (test 500-520 eV).

This setup will fully relax both the cell shape/volume and ionic positions of bulk FCC Cu (ISIF=3). Cu is metallic so ISMEAR=1 (Methfessel-Paxton) with SIGMA=0.1 is used. The k-point mesh of 12×12×12 provides good convergence for the FCC structure (approximately 0.025 Å⁻¹ spacing). After completion, the optimized lattice constant can be read from the final lattice vectors in CONTCAR - for a cubic system, it will be the a-axis length. The experimental lattice constant of Cu is ~3.615 Å; PBE typically slightly overestimates this by ~1-2%. Cu is not magnetic in its ground state so ISPIN=2 is not needed.

This calculation will fully relax both the cell shape/volume (ISIF=3) and ionic positions of rock-salt MgO. The system is an insulator, so ISMEAR=0 (Gaussian) with SIGMA=0.05 is used for the relaxation. ENCUT=520 eV provides good convergence for both Mg and O. The 8x8x8 Gamma-centered k-point mesh should give energy convergence better than 1 meV/atom. The optimized lattice constant can be extracted from the final CONTCAR file (diagonal elements of the lattice vectors should be equal for cubic symmetry). Experimental lattice constant is ~4.21 Å; PBE typically overestimates by ~1-2%. After relaxation completes, check that forces are below 0.01 eV/Å and that the structure maintains cubic symmetry.

This calculation will fully relax bulk diamond (both cell shape/volume and ionic positions). ISIF=3 allows full cell optimization. ISMEAR=0 (Gaussian smearing) is used because diamond is an insulator with a large band gap. The 8x8x8 Gamma-centered k-point mesh provides good convergence for the cubic cell (reciprocal spacing ~0.036 1/Å). After completion, check the CONTCAR file for the optimized structure - the lattice constant will be the first lattice vector length. The experimental lattice constant for diamond is ~3.567 Å, so expect a value close to this (PBE typically overestimates by ~1-2%). The symmetry will preserve the cubic structure, so all three lattice vectors should remain equal. Verify convergence by checking that forces (EDIFFG=-0.01) and stress tensor are small in the final ionic step.
